Write a resolution. Committee: DISEC. Topic: Military intervention Red Sea. Main submitter: unspecified.

Recognises the tumultuous situation regarding the Red Sea crisis
Reaffirms the importance of adopting a multi-pronged approach to address the issue of piracy holistically
Condemns the attacks on 100+ vessels transiting the Red Sea
Urges for countries to monitor ships traversing international and national waterways

This council therefore,

1. Demands for international military intervention in the vicinity of the Red sea, particularly on the Yemeni waterline, implementing enhanced naval operations with the regional governments, for purposes such as but not limited to:
a. The dismantling and eradication of pirate mother ships via means of effective enforcement, such as but not limited to:
i. Real-time satellite tracking of vessels traversing the Red Sea
ii. The deployment of enhanced drone surveillance
iii. Joint patrols with regional navies under the Djibouti Code framework
b. to provide LEDCs prone to Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, such as Yemen, Djibouti and other countries, such as but not limited to, and in the name of self-defense:
i. Frigates
ii. Warships
iii. Destroyers
iv. Cruisers
v. Missile and weapons systems
c. to create job opportunities in the rebuilt Navy for the unemployed population within affected regions, inclusive of but not conclusively
i. recruit and train the unemployed citizens to work in the navy
ii. Provide resources for long term training towards the new recruits lpp
d. to secure areas prone to attacks from Houthis and Somali pirates, such as but not limited to
i. the coast of Yemen
ii. the Gulf of Aden
iii. the Red Sea
iv. the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait

2. Dismantle pirate mother ships and the piracy network using effective enforcement of real-life satellite imagery data;
a. utilize satellite imagery from systems including but not limited to:
i. Utilization of China's Beidou satellite systems, United States's GPS systems to coordinate for pirate motherships
ii. Track pirate motherships on satellite systems, detecting ships and vessels with suspicious actions such as repeatedly boarding individuals from smaller vessels or boats that are linked to the motherships
b. Navigating the suspected or targeted pirate motherships previously on the satellite systems, collaborating with local coast guards, responding to the satellite imagery swiftly, operating as follows:
i. Coast guards equipped with optical sighting systems observe suspected vessels from a safe distance of 500-1000 meters varying depending on weather conditions
ii. Once confirmed to be a malicious mothership, coast guards respond immediately to coastal defenses, immediately deploying reinforcements to the mothership locations on waters and dismantle the mothership
iii. Funding for optical sighting systems and coastal guard forces provided by United Nations
c. Ensuring the safe use of satellites through legislation and information sharing with regional governments
i. Satellites systems such as GPS or Beidou technologies shared with trusted DISEC committee, operating under United Nations control to prevent insecurity and enhance reliability of satellites uses
ii. All information gathered are to be shared real time to local governments whose territorial waters are closest to the mothership location, assuming location is on international waters

3. Strongly urges for countries to monitor ships on international waters;
a. Calls for MDCs to utilise satellites to allow quick tracking of suspicious ships
b. Calls for the making of the REAL department
c. Rewards — if helmsmen successful marine vessels, they
i. Get 1 month of tax exception
ii. 30% off for buying ship fuel across UN countries, funded by parties including but not limited to the IMF or volunteering countries
d. App — development of an app that allows helmsmen to report unauthorized or suspicious ships which can be tracked of satellites
e. Licence — Developing a UN-ified licence with a trial period of 10 years for authorising ships, complete with a database to keep data of UN approved ships
i. Unauthorised ships to not be allowed on waters
ii. Once these unauthorised blocs are reported through app and subjected to legal procedures regarding validity of its status as authorised
f. Establishes security corridors, expanding the Internationaly Recommended Transit Corridor (IRTC) in the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea and the Bab Al-Mandab Strait:
i. Initially a 6-month voluntary, pilot programme
ii. Armed escort vessels would patrol these corridors under a joint mandate by conducted by the UNCTAD and the IMO, with consent from coastal states
iii. Armed security operating under code of conduct by the IMO can be sourced from private companies, national militaries
iv. Funded by The IMO's International Maritime Security Trust Fund (IMST) and a 10% windfall tax on profits of the top 50 transnational shipping companies

4. Addresses the rehabilitation or reintegration of captured pirates through methods such as;
a. Enforcing the enrollment of ex-pirates in skilled, sea-related, and peaceful occupations, such as but not limited to,
i. Naval navigation and exploration of underdeveloped sea zones
ii. Sharing of intelligence with international anti-piracy forces
iii. Support in establishing and protecting legal, anti-piracy businesses
iv. Preventing ex-pirates from having access to arms by escorting these missions using recognized, armed escort ships consisting of local naval police forces, trained through UN capacity building programs
b. Re-allocating money from seized pirate assets to
i. Communities with a high risk of piracy
ii. Educational programs for the younger generations
iii. Providing salary bonuses to enrolled ex-pirates
c. Providing training and education programs in rehabilitation centers for the effective return to the community and providing services such as
i. Providing skill-set acquisition necessary for blue-collar to white collar occupations, including but not limited to proficiency with technology and a minimum of a grade 7 education
ii. Regular examination and reflection on effectiveness
d. Encouraging rehabilitated pirates to join occupations of any kind with the exception of occupations related to security or those that bear arms
i. Individuals with a criminal record of maritime piracy shall be rejected from such occupations, despite having undergone rehabilitation programs

5. Urges member states to provide essential aids to regional countries and provide long-term assistance with the mechanism which overseas and regulates the usage and allocation of the capital, such as but not limited to,
a. Short-term aids,
i. Funds
ii. Technological equipment and resources,
iii. Medical equipment,
iv. Manpower and labor resources
b. Long-term remedies
i. Education of the general public,
ii. J*b opportunities
iii. Training for police and military forces
c. Strengthen Governance and Judicial systems, calling for:
i. Legal reforms
ii. Fair prosecution
iii. UNODC expansion
iv. Capacity ownership reform

Write a resolution. Committee: Disarmament and International Security Council. Topic: Addressing Issues Related to Maritime Piracy in the Middle East and Northern Africa. Main submitter: United Arab Emirates.

Strongly discourages non-Middle Eastern and Northern African nations to deploy naval forces to the region without UN backing or diplomatic contact with GCC states,
Having considered past successful operations on pnaval patrol in the Middle East and North Africa —f;
Welcoming international cooperation and naval support to ensure the safety and prosperity of Middle Eastern and North African shipping channels
Reaffirming the need to address the root causes of the piracy problem

1. Calls for regional powers to cooperate on combating maritime piracy, with methods including but not limited to:
a. Increasing state-led basic coastal patrols in pirate infested waters
b. Divert defence budget towards coastal defences, including but not limited to:
i. Increasing training exercises with all vessels in the region
ii. Increase the amount of vessels in the region
c. Cooperating with foreign naval powers to support GCC-led naval patrols for key shipments, by ways including but not limited to:
i. Energy resources
ii. Humanitarian aid
d. Establishing a Joint Task Force with navies in the Middle East and North Africa to increase cooperation in patrolling the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden within GCC states
e. Encourage UN member states to offer maritime interdiction expertise to train regional coast guards and navies

2. Encourages the regulation of armed private security personnel on commercial ships, in ways such as but not limited to;
a. Establishing a UN-backed certification system for private armed personnel, mandating:
i. Strict protocol regarding use of force
ii. Basic UN training required
iii. Armed personal accountable towards the ship's origin's jurisdiction
iv. Transparency in contracts to avoid mercenary activities
b. Require the information armed personnel onboard commercial ship to be uploaded for UN review,
c. Reject personal with previous conviction from being employed for security on commercial ship

3. Attempting to raise a fund managed by the UN to reform poverty regions in coastal communities, in ways such as but not limited to;
a. Funding a minimum of $200 million in a year to be raised through either grants or loans, by organisations such as but not limited to;
i. An annual trust fund financed by canal tolls
ii. World Bank
iii. MEDCs
iv. IMF
b. Allocating funding to create a sustainable fishery project to protect local fishermen of their employment;
i. Ensuring foreign corporations do not pollute waters which would make local fishermen lose their only source of income
ii. Prevent exploitation of local fishermen so their product are not sold at a below-average price
iii. Collaborate with NGOs to bring these changes to the people in need
c. Encouraging LEDC governments to take Colombia's PDET program as a reference when implementing reforms, in ways such as but not limited to;
i. Fostering community ownership such as by involving village leaders to decide on infrastructure developments in the area
ii. Increasing locals' trust in the government
iii. Offering job opportunities to locals in extreme poverty
d. Create an oversight committee under the UNSC to ensure that funds are distributed for their original intention, in ways such as but not limited to;
i. Allocation of funds to be tied with the reduction of illicit economic activity
ii. Mandate real time documentation of fund distribution
iii. Eligibility of funds to be reviewed every quarter of the year

4. Ensures every former pirate a job for survival instead of committing criminal activities after rehabilitation, in ways such as but not limited to:
a. The construction of major infrastructure that connects countries and regions, with funding addressed from the previous clause, such as but a not limited to:
i. Railways
ii. International airports
iii. Sea ports
b. A monitoring body will be created to ensure that former pirates will no longer return to their criminal ways, details are listed in below:
i. Create a probation program for ex-criminals in which they are required to check in with an office each month for monitoring purposes

5. Amends international laws to combat maritime piracy and its nearby issues, including but not limited to
a. Expanding the Djibouti Code of Conduct to ban arms trafficking and illicit weapon trade
b. Adjusting the basic provisions of universal jurisdiction over piracy and refining the relevant measures in exercising that jurisdiction to prosecute pirates, including but not limited to:
i. Encourage the updating domestic laws to criminalize all armed robbery at sea under United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)
ii. Clarify whether offences that may constitute as independent crimes fall under universal jurisdiction
iii. Reinforce the provisions of Article 58 (3) and Article (2) of UNCLOS, requiring coastal states and other states to make joint efforts to take into account each other's rights and obligations

i. Promote African intra-regional financing alternatives, such as but not limited to the African Export-Import Bank, the New Development Bank and regional pooling of resources

5. Require past colonizers who have previously exploited Africa to slowly pay reparations (from their own national income)

Write a resolution. Committee: Disarmament and International Security Committee. Topic: Discussing Oil's Role as a Conflict Instigator in Conflict Zones. Main submitter: Republic of Belarus.

PREAMBLE:

Affirming the importance of tralalero trala,
Recognising the need to address how oil resources can be used to instigate conflict,
Acknowledging the heinous crimes of the Islamic Republic of Iran
Investing in the economic diversification of petrostates and other LICs

1. Creation of the intergovernmental organisation TRALALERO (Transparency and Resilience Alliance for Leveraging Alternatives, Liquidity, and Economic Reform of Oil) consisting of a neutral, multilateral body of organs and:
a. Forming partnerships linking developed nations with the Global South in relation to the energy sector:
i. Establishing Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to ensure security through development
ii. Ensuring local job creation, inhibiting the breeding ground for extremism
iii. Direct investment in connectivity infrastructure, including roads, bridges and energy infrastructure
iv. Integration of marginalised communities into the formal economy

b. Trade must be shielded from the economic landmines or otherwise sanctions for reasons such as, but not limited to:

c. Integration of national development plans to guide the usage of funds

ii. Enhance intelligence sharing
